defects: Requires f to be a continuous linear map (E →L[R] F) instead of gold's plain (possibly discontinuous) linear map (E →ₗ[𝕜] F); this adds a continuity hypothesis absent from the gold statement, changing the theorem's content

Drops the topological-vector-space structure: gold requires IsTopologicalAddGroup and ContinuousSMul on both E and F, produced only assumes bare TopologicalSpace with no compatibility between the topology and the algebraic/module structure
Replaces the NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜 with CompleteSpace 𝕜 by an arbitrary Semiring R, losing the normed-field/completeness structure that the theorem's classical proof relies on
Uses AddCommMonoid instead of AddCommGroup for E and F, a weaker algebraic hypothesis than gold's AddCommGroup
Overall these changes make the produced statement a different (not clearly equivalent) proposition rather than a faithful restatement of the gold theorem
